title: ioctl_key_export_private: second call replaces outbuf without draining first
description: ioctl_key_export_private() unconditionally replaces state->outbuf with a new kmalloc buffer containing the private key bytes, even if outbuf already contains data from a previous KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE call that was not fully drained. The old outbuf is zeroized and freed (correct for key material), but if it contained partially-drained private key bytes, those bytes are permanently lost. A userspace caller who calls KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE, reads partial bytes, calls KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE again (perhaps by accident), loses the unread portion of the first export. This is a data loss scenario for key material. The second export produces fresh bytes from key_export_private(), so the caller gets the full key from the second call — but they may not realize the first partial read was invalidated. More subtly: the outbuf replacement also discards any bytes from a public key that was being read (since KEY fd read() first drains outbuf if non-empty). After KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE, subsequent read() calls that were expecting to get the public key will instead get the (partially drained) private key bytes. Trigger: KEY_GENERATE → read(partial public key) → KEY_EXPORT_PRIVATE → outbuf replaced with private key → subsequent read() returns private key bytes, not remaining public key bytes.
close_reason: fixed: added EBUSY guard (outbuf && outbuf_drained < outbuf_len) before allowing second export in ioctl_key_export_private
